title: Blink LED
description: Verify the USB path, board profile, bootloader, compile, upload, and sketch execution.
notes: Verify the onboard L LED, not the always-on power LED.
boundary: This verifies the programming path only; it is not a sensor measurement.

title: Synthetic Signal
description: Generate a 0.5 Hz sine wave at 50 Hz to verify Arduino → serial → BetterBoard → measurement export without a sensor.
boundary: Synthetic data validates the software path, not experimental accuracy.

title: Bench 01 — Analog Control & Instrumentation
description: Turn a potentiometer or other known-safe low-voltage analog source into a complete input → ADC → filtering → PWM command → live measurement workflow.
hardware: potentiometer or known-safe low-voltage analog source on A0
optional LED with suitable series resistor on PWM pin D9
notes: Built-in LED turns on above 50% normalized input.
D9 outputs a 0–255 PWM command proportional to the calibrated normalized input.
The reported voltage is nominal until the real ADC reference/input path is characterized.
boundary: Use only inputs within the board's supported analog range. Nominal voltage, filtering, and endpoint scaling do not by themselves establish calibration accuracy or traceability.

title: 3-axis Magnetic Field
description: Acquire Bx, By, Bz and a configurable primary axis from an MLX90393 at 20 Hz.
notes: Control sensor orientation, scan path, and distance reference for magnet comparisons.
boundary: Magnetic-field acquisition does not establish calibration traceability or model validity.

title: 3-axis Acceleration
description: Acquire ax, ay, az and a configurable primary axis from an ADXL345 at 100 Hz.
hardware: ADXL345 accelerometer or a later confirmed compatible replacement
notes: The user's photographed XYZ module has not yet been confirmed as ADXL345.
boundary: Mechanical-honeycomb measurements are an analogue experiment, not direct graphene validation.

title: Photogate Timer
description: Timestamp falling-edge events, reject very close duplicate edges, and report period and frequency.
notes: Uses INPUT_PULLUP and a falling-edge interrupt on D2.
Minimum edge spacing is 2 ms in the canonical firmware.
boundary: Frequency accuracy depends on the sensor, geometry, event definition, and clock behavior.

title: Quadrature Encoder
description: Track quadrature counts on D2/D3 and convert counts to angle at 100 Hz.
notes: COUNTS_PER_REVOLUTION=600 is a placeholder and must match the actual encoder.
boundary: Angle is only calibrated when counts-per-revolution and mechanical coupling are known.

title: Pulse / RPM
description: Measure pulse periods and convert them to RPM using a configurable pulses-per-revolution constant.
notes: PULSES_PER_REVOLUTION defaults to 1 and must be configured for the real sensor.
boundary: RPM accuracy depends on pulses-per-revolution and sensor/event quality.

title: Random Walk Robot
description: Run conservative, bounded stochastic low-speed commands for a two-motor tabletop robot.
hardware: two small low-voltage DC gear motors
physical_lab_targets: Random Walk & Monte Carlo physical experiment
notes: Motor-driver pin assignments are placeholders until the exact driver is identified.
Actual x(t), y(t) should come from independent position measurement such as camera/object tracking.
boundary: Motor command duration is not a measured trajectory or displacement.

title: I²C Scanner
description: Scan 7-bit I²C addresses to help identify whether a connected I²C device responds.
notes: Diagnostic output is intentionally textual and should not be registered as Measurement Evidence.
boundary: An address response identifies bus communication only; it does not prove the exact sensor model or correct calibration.
